questions.question: A financial services company is hosting a multi-tier web application on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances, and an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database in the backend. Security policy dictates that database credentials must be rotated automatically every 30 days without application downtime, and the credentials must never be hardcoded in the application code or configuration files.

options.text: Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a SecureString. Use a cron job on the EC2 instances to update the database password every 30 days and update the Parameter Store value accordingly.
Hardcode the initial database credentials in the application environment variables using AWS CloudFormation, and update the CloudFormation stack parameters every 30 days to rotate the credentials.

Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure an AWS Lambda rotation function using Secrets Manager to automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Configure the EC2 instances to retrieve the credentials dynamically from Secrets Manager at runtime using an IAM instance profile.

Store the database credentials in an Amazon S3 bucket encrypted with AWS KMS. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to trigger an AWS Lambda function every 30 days to update the S3 object and the RDS password.

questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the optimal service for managing database credentials. It provides built-in rotation capabilities via AWS Lambda templates and allows secure retrieval at runtime without exposing credentials in code or plain text configuration.

wrongOptionNotes.A: While Parameter Store supports SecureString, it does not provide native automated rotation integration like Secrets Manager does, requiring custom complex scheduling and orchestration scripts prone to failure.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Hardcoding credentials or relying on manual CloudFormation stack updates violates security best practices and causes application downtime during stack updates and instance reboots.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Storing database credentials inside an S3 bucket introduces unnecessary architectural overhead, security risks regarding bucket policies, and lacks the specialized lifecycle and rotation management features of Secrets Manager.

questions.question: A healthcare startup stores patient records in Amazon S3 buckets. Compliance regulations require that all data objects must be encrypted at rest using keys managed by the company, and the company must have complete control over key rotation, key policies, and auditing key usage via AWS CloudTrail. The solution must minimize operational complexity.

options.text: Deploy an external hardware security module (HSM) on-premises, connect it to AWS using AWS Direct Connect, and configure S3 to use client-side encryption with keys generated on the on-premises HSM.
Use AWS KMS customer managed keys (CMKs) to encrypt the S3 buckets. Configure automatic annual key rotation for the CMKs and define strict key policies.
Use AWS KMS AWS managed keys for encrypting the S3 buckets. Enable multi-Region replication and custom key policies.
Use Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) for encrypting the buckets, and write custom scripts to re-encrypt the data every year.

questions.explanation: AWS KMS customer managed keys (CMKs) allow organizations to maintain full administrative control, auditability through CloudTrail, and configure automatic key rotation while leveraging fully managed cloud infrastructure.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Client-side encryption with an on-premises HSM introduces extreme operational complexity, latency, and management overhead that is unnecessary when AWS KMS CMKs provide cloud-native control.
wrongOptionNotes.C: AWS managed keys are managed by AWS services on behalf of the customer, and customers cannot modify key policies or control key rotation schedules.
wrongOptionNotes.D: SSE-S3 uses keys managed entirely by AWS, meaning the customer does not have control over key policies or custom rotation schedules.

questions.question: An enterprise web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances inside a private subnet. The application needs to occasionally make API calls to Amazon DynamoDB and download patches from an external public repository on the internet. Security policy dictates that the EC2 instances must never be exposed to inbound traffic from the internet, and outbound traffic to the internet must be strictly controlled and audited.

options.text: Attach an Internet Gateway (IGW) directly to the private subnet route table, and use Network ACLs to block all inbound traffic while allowing outbound traffic.
Deploy a public-facing Application Load Balancer in front of the private EC2 instances, and configure security groups to block all outbound traffic.

Use an Amazon VPC endpoint (Gateway type) for DynamoDB to route traffic securely within the AWS network. Route internet-bound traffic through a centralized inspection VPC containing third-party firewall appliances accessed via a Transit Gateway.
Configure a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, route outbound traffic from the private subnet through the NAT Gateway, and use Interface VPC endpoints for DynamoDB.

questions.explanation: VPC endpoints keep traffic to AWS services within the AWS backbone network, while secure outbound internet access is best managed through centralized architectures such as inspection VPCs behind firewalls or controlled egress proxies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Attaching an IGW directly to a private subnet converts it effectively into a public subnet, violating the security policy that prohibits direct internet exposure.
wrongOptionNotes.B: An ALB is for inbound traffic distribution and does not solve the requirement for outbound internet access to download patches.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While a NAT Gateway and Interface VPC endpoints work technically, routing all general internet traffic through a standard NAT Gateway does not provide the advanced centralized traffic inspection and strict firewall auditing required by enterprise security policies compared to a dedicated inspection VPC.

questions.question: A media company is developing an AWS Lambda function that processes sensitive video metadata and writes output to an Amazon S3 bucket. The security team requires that the Lambda function execute with the absolute minimum set of permissions necessary to perform its specific tasks.

options.text: Attach the AmazonS3FullAccess managed policy to the Lambda execution role so it can access any S3 bucket in the account.
Use the AWS account root user credentials embedded in the Lambda environment variables to authorize access to Amazon S3.

Create a dedicated IAM execution role for the Lambda function. Attach a policy granting s3:PutObject permission exclusively on the specific target S3 bucket ARN and its contents, and attach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole for CloudWatch Logs.
Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to the Lambda execution role to ensure the function never fails due to permission errors.

questions.explanation: Adhering to the principle of least privilege involves creating dedicated IAM roles with resource-scoped policies granting only the specific actions and resources required for operation.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AmazonS3FullAccess provides overly broad permissions across all buckets in the account, failing the least privilege requirement.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Embedding root credentials in environment variables is an extreme security anti-pattern and violates fundamental AWS security standards.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Using AdministratorAccess grants unrestricted permissions to all AWS resources, severely violating the principle of least privilege and introducing massive security risks.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform hosted on AWS experiences occasional web application attacks, including SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). The security architect needs a scalable solution to inspect incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic and automatically block these malicious web requests before they reach the Application Load Balancer.

options.text: Deploy AWS Shield Advanced and enable automatic mitigation for Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks.
Deploy AWS WAF and associate it with the Application Load Balancer. Configure AWS Managed Rules rule groups for SQL injection and cross-site scripting protection.
Configure Amazon GuardDuty with custom IP set filters to block malicious IP addresses from connecting to the Application Load Balancer.
Implement Amazon Inspector vulnerability scanning on the EC2 instances behind the Application Load Balancer.

questions.explanation: AWS WAF protects web applications by allowing you to create security rules that control bot traffic and block common attack patterns such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting.

wrongOptionNotes.A: While AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks at layers 3 and 4 (and integrates with WAF for layer 7), AWS WAF is specifically required to define rules for inspecting and blocking application-layer threats like SQLi and XSS.
wrongOptionNotes.C: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events, but it does not inspect HTTP layer payloads or block web application attacks like SQLi and XSS directly at the load balancer.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon Inspector assesses EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and network reachability, not real-time HTTP web traffic filtering.

questions.question: A multinational corporation has hundreds of AWS accounts managed centrally via AWS Organizations. The security operations team requires visibility into security alerts and potential account compromises across all accounts, with the ability to aggregate findings into a single designated administrator account.

options.text: Deploy Amazon Inspector agents on every EC2 instance across all accounts and configure them to send alerts via Amazon SNS to the security team's email.
Create custom IAM cross-account roles in every account, and have a script running in the central account poll CloudWatch alarms from each spoke account.
Configure AWS CloudTrail in each member account to deliver logs to an S3 bucket in the central account, and write custom AWS Lambda scripts to analyze the logs for security threats.
Enable Amazon GuardDuty across all member accounts within AWS Organizations and designate a central security account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator.

questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty supports multi-account management through AWS Organizations and delegated administrator functionality, enabling centralized aggregation of security findings.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Amazon Inspector focuses on vulnerability assessments rather than continuous account-level threat detection (such as unusual API calls, malicious IPs, or crypto-mining) across all AWS accounts.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Polling CloudWatch alarms via custom cross-account roles is inefficient, difficult to scale, and lacks intelligent threat aggregation capabilities.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Building and maintaining custom scripts to analyze CloudTrail logs for real-time threat intelligence introduces high operational overhead and duplicates built-in security services.

questions.question: An enterprise application stores confidential documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Compliance regulations require that all objects written to the bucket must be encrypted, and the S3 bucket policy must explicitly deny any upload requests that do not specify server-side encryption.

options.text: Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket using Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).

Configure an S3 bucket policy with a condition that denies requests (`StringNotEquals` or `Null`) where `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` is missing or does not match the approved encryption type (e.g., `AES256` or `aws:kms`).
Configure AWS Trusted Advisor to scan the bucket daily and delete any unencrypted objects found.
Attach an IAM policy to every user granting `s3:PutObject` while restricting them from using other services.

questions.explanation: Enforcing encryption at upload requires a preventative S3 bucket policy with an explicit `Deny` statement checking for missing or incorrect `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` header values.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Default encryption ensures that objects are encrypted when saved, but it does not block a client from explicitly requesting an unencrypted upload unless enforced via a bucket policy Deny condition.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on a periodic scan to delete unencrypted objects leaves a compliance window open and is reactive rather than preventative.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Relying solely on IAM user policies is harder to maintain at scale and does not provide resource-level preventative enforcement against anonymous or cross-account uploads compared to an S3 bucket policy.

questions.question: A financial institution requires that all API calls made to AWS services across their AWS Organization must be logged, and the log files stored in Amazon S3 must be continuously checked for tampering or unauthorized modifications. The solution must be tamper-proof.

options.text: Enable an AWS CloudTrail trail across all accounts in AWS Organizations with log file validation enabled. Store the logs in an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled in Compliance mode.
Enable AWS CloudTrail and restrict access to the S3 bucket using IAM policies that deny delete actions to standard developers.
Store CloudTrail logs in Amazon EBS encrypted volumes attached to an EC2 instance, and take daily snapshots.
Configure AWS CloudTrail in the management account, and set up an Amazon SNS topic to alert administrators whenever a log file is deleted from S3.

questions.explanation: Combining CloudTrail log file validation (cryptographic checksums) with S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode provides immutable, tamper-proof audit log storage.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Standard IAM policies can be modified by administrators or root users, failing to provide the ultimate immutability guarantee offered by S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Storing CloudTrail logs on EBS volumes is inefficient, operationally burdensome, and lacks native log integrity validation features.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Alerting after deletion is reactive and does not prevent tampering or fulfill strict compliance mandates for immutable audit logs.

questions.question: A software development team needs to deploy applications onto Amazon EC2 instances. Security policy requires that administrators must never have interactive SSH or RDP access to production instances, yet engineers must still be able to securely troubleshoot applications or inspect logs interactively when necessary.

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to establish secure, audited interactive shell sessions to the EC2 instances over HTTPS without requiring open inbound ports or SSH keys.
Configure AWS Client VPN to connect engineers to the VPC, and assign public IP addresses to all production instances for direct SSH access.
Deploy a bastion host (jump box) in a public subnet, open security group port 22 from the corporate IP to the bastion, and allow SSH forwarding to private instances.
Embed temporary SSH public keys into the EC2 instance metadata service via user data scripts upon every reboot.

questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure, managed remote access to EC2 instances without needing inbound ports open, bastion hosts, or SSH key management.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Assigning public IP addresses to production instances and allowing direct SSH access dramatically increases the security risk and attack surface.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Bastion hosts require managing SSH keys and maintaining open inbound port 22, increasing the attack surface and violating the requirement to eliminate traditional interactive shell access paths.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Managing SSH keys manually or via user data scripts remains prone to key sprawl and does not provide the audited session management controls of Session Manager.

questions.question: An enterprise is setting up a hybrid cloud architecture connecting its on-premises datacenter to AWS using an AWS Direct Connect connection. The security team insists that all data traversing the Direct Connect link must be encrypted in transit using IPsec tunnels.

options.text: Configure AWS Direct Connect with an AWS Transit Gateway or Virtual Private Gateway, and establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection running over the Direct Connect public virtual interface or AWS Direct Connect SiteLink.
Configure Amazon CloudFront with HTTPS enabled between the on-premises datacenter and AWS.
Attach an SSL certificate directly to the Direct Connect router on-premises and enable TLS encryption on the physical fiber optic cables.
Enable MACsec on the AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection ports to encrypt traffic natively at Layer 2.

questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect private virtual interfaces do not encrypt data by default. To achieve encryption in transit, organizations establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection or use MACsec where available.

wrongOptionNotes.B: CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network designed for caching and delivering web content to end-user clients, not for hybrid datacenter connectivity.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Direct Connect operates at Layer 2/3 of the OSI model and does not support attaching SSL certificates directly to physical links or fiber optic cables.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While MACsec is supported on specific Direct Connect locations for MACsec-capable ports, pairing a Site-to-Site VPN over Direct Connect is the standard architectural pattern for end-to-end IPsec encryption across virtual networks.

questions.question: A global enterprise has resources distributed across multiple AWS accounts and regions. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) wants a single, centralized dashboard that aggregates security findings, evaluates compliance against industry benchmarks (such as CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark), and provides automated remediation guidance.

options.text: Use Amazon Macie across all accounts to generate security findings and export them to an Amazon S3 bucket for manual analysis.
Create custom Amazon CloudWatch Dashboards in every AWS account, and write custom metric filters for all security log groups.
Enable AWS Security Hub, designate a central management account, and configure cross-account aggregation to consolidate security findings and compliance status into a single dashboard.
Deploy AWS Trusted Advisor in the management account only, and share its reports via email weekly.

questions.explanation: AWS Security Hub is designed to provide a comprehensive view of your security state across AWS accounts and check your environment against security industry standards and best practices.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Amazon Macie focuses specifically on discovering and protecting sensitive data (like PII) in S3, whereas Security Hub provides a comprehensive multi-account security and compliance dashboard.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Building custom CloudWatch dashboards across hundreds of accounts lacks automated compliance standards checking and requires massive maintenance overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Trusted Advisor provides high-level checks but does not offer centralized multi-account security finding aggregation and continuous compliance standard evaluations like Security Hub.

questions.question: A financial application stores Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in Amazon S3 buckets. The security team needs an automated solution to continuously discover, classify, and protect sensitive data stored in S3 without manual intervention.

options.text: Configure AWS Config rules to check whether S3 buckets have public access blocked and whether default encryption is enabled.

Enable Amazon Macie across the AWS accounts. Configure Macie jobs to inspect S3 buckets for sensitive data such as PII, credit card numbers, and credentials, and review the generated security findings.
Write custom Python scripts using boto3 to download every file from Amazon S3 daily, parse the text locally, and search for regex patterns representing PII.
Enable Amazon S3 server access logging and analyze the log files using Amazon Athena to identify which users accessed PII files.

questions.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to automatically discover, classify, and report on sensitive data such as PII stored in Amazon S3.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS Config validates resource configurations and compliance posture, but it does not scan object content for sensitive data classification like Amazon Macie does.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Writing custom scripts to download and parse data at scale introduces severe performance bottlenecks, high network costs, and security risks regarding data handling.
wrongOptionNotes.D: S3 access logs track who accessed which objects, but they do not scan the actual file contents to discover and classify sensitive data types like PII.

questions.question: An organization is designing a web application using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. To protect against unauthorized access, the security architect wants to implement token-based authentication where clients authenticate with an identity provider, receive a JSON Web Token (JWT), and present that token to API Gateway for authorization.

options.text: Use AWS IAM authentication for all public-facing client requests by embedding AWS IAM long-term access keys into the client mobile and web applications.
Write a custom AWS Lambda function to inspect the raw TCP payload of every incoming request to API Gateway and manually decrypt the SSL certificate.
Store client usernames and passwords in plain text in an Amazon DynamoDB table, and have the Lambda function query DynamoDB on every request to verify credentials.
Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool or a third-party OpenID Connect (OIDC) compliant identity provider, and attach a JWT authorizer to the API Gateway HTTP API or REST API routes.

questions.explanation: API Gateway JWT authorizers provide scalable, serverless token validation by integrating with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC identity providers like Amazon Cognito.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Embedding long-term AWS IAM credentials in client-side mobile or web applications is a critical security vulnerability because users can decompile the app and extract the keys.
wrongOptionNotes.B: API Gateway handles TLS termination and ingress handling; writing custom TCP inspection code is unnecessary and architecturally impossible.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Storing credentials in plain text in DynamoDB violates basic security practices, and verifying passwords on every request introduces severe performance latency.

questions.question: A company is deploying an application on Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC. The security team mandates that any network traffic attempting to traverse between different subnets within the same VPC must be filtered at the subnet boundary with stateless rule evaluation.

options.text: Implement AWS WAF Web ACLs attached to the VPC route tables.
Deploy AWS Shield Standard and enable automatic route table modifications for blocked subnets.
Configure Amazon EC2 Security Groups attached to the elastic network interfaces (ENIs) of the instances.

Configure Amazon VPC Network Access Control Lists (Network ACLs) associated with the subnets, defining explicit stateless allow and deny rules based on IP protocols, ports, and source/destination CIDR blocks.

questions.explanation: Network ACLs act as a stateless firewall at the subnet level, evaluating inbound and outbound traffic against explicit rules, whereas Security Groups act as stateful firewalls at the instance level.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS WAF filters web application traffic (Layer 7) and cannot be attached to VPC route tables for subnet-level packet filtering.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS Shield provides automated DDoS protection and does not perform stateless subnet-to-subnet traffic filtering.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Security Groups operate at the instance level (ENI), are stateful, and evaluate traffic before it reaches or leaves the specific instance, not at the subnet boundary.

questions.question: An enterprise developer accidentally committed an AWS IAM user's long-term access key and secret access key into a public code repository on GitHub. An automated monitoring bot detected the leak within minutes. What is the most immediate, high-priority action the security team should take?

options.text: Delete the GitHub repository and wait 24 hours for AWS automated scanning to invalidate the credentials automatically.
Delete the entire AWS account immediately and restore all infrastructure from backups in a new account.
Deactivate and delete the compromised IAM access key immediately in the AWS IAM console or via AWS CLI, then investigate CloudTrail logs to determine if unauthorized API calls were made.
Attach an explicit Deny IAM policy to the compromised user's account while keeping the access key active for debugging purposes.

questions.explanation: When credentials are leaked, the immediate priority is to deactivate and delete the compromised access keys to prevent unauthorized access, followed by investigating CloudTrail logs to assess potential impact.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS does not automatically invalidate leaked keys based on external repository scans without manual intervention, leaving the account vulnerable during the 24-hour window.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Deleting the entire AWS account is an extreme, disproportionate response when simply revoking the compromised access key resolves the immediate threat.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Keeping compromised access keys active while modifying policies is risky because leaked keys can still be used to bypass certain policy assumptions or perform valid actions not explicitly denied.

questions.question: A company is running an application on Amazon EC2 instances within a private VPC subnet. The instances occasionally require patches and software updates from external repositories on the public internet. However, security policy strictly prohibits these EC2 instances from having inbound access from the internet or exposing public IP addresses. How should a Solutions Architect design outbound internet access to meet these requirements?

options.text: Attach an Internet Gateway to the VPC, assign Elastic IP addresses to the EC2 instances, and configure security groups to block all inbound traffic.
Configure an egress-only internet gateway in the private subnet and update the security groups to allow outbound traffic.
Deploy a NAT instance in the private subnet, and configure the default route to point to the NAT instance.
Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, and configure the route table of the private subnet to direct outbound internet-bound traffic to the NAT Gateway.

questions.explanation: To enable outbound internet connectivity for private EC2 instances without exposing them to inbound threats, a NAT Gateway must be deployed in a public subnet. The private subnet's route table is then updated to point traffic destined for 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway. This ensures stateful outbound communication while maintaining complete isolation from inbound internet traffic.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Assigning Elastic IP addresses exposes instances to the public internet via public IPv4 addresses, which violates the security policy.
wrongOptionNotes.B: An egress-only internet gateway is exclusively used for IPv6 traffic, whereas standard VPC private subnets often require IPv4 connectivity for legacy repositories.
wrongOptionNotes.C: NAT instances must be placed in a public subnet with an Internet Gateway to function properly; placing them in a private subnet prevents external communication.

questions.question: An enterprise maintains a central logging AWS account and numerous application accounts managed through AWS Organizations. Application teams generate extensive Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The security team mandates that all log data must be aggregated into the central logging account's Amazon S3 bucket securely, with minimal administrative overhead. What is the most scalable architectural approach to achieve this?

options.text: Write a custom AWS Lambda function in each application account to query CloudWatch Logs periodically and upload the logs to the central S3 bucket.

Configure CloudWatch Logs subscription filters in each application account to stream log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream or directly to an Amazon SNS topic that invokes an AWS Lambda function in the central account.
Configure cross-account Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams from each application account directly to the central logging account's S3 bucket.

Use CloudWatch Logs cross-account subscription filters to stream log data from each application account to an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream or an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose in the central logging account, which then writes to the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs subscription filters support streaming log events cross-account to a centralized destination such as Kinesis Data Streams or Kinesis Data Firehose in a security or logging account. This eliminates the need for polling scripts or complex custom infrastructure, scaling efficiently across hundreds of accounts.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Building and maintaining custom polling Lambda functions introduces unnecessary complexity, latency, and operational overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.B: This architecture requires maintaining intermediary streaming resources and custom ingestion logic, increasing operational burden compared to native features.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While possible, managing individual Kinesis streams per account is more complex and expensive than using native CloudWatch subscription filters.

questions.question: A financial institution requires that any sensitive data stored in Amazon S3 must be encrypted using customer-provided keys or keys managed by AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Furthermore, the security team must maintain absolute control over the rotation and key policies, and needs to track every usage of the encryption keys via AWS CloudTrail. Which configuration satisfies these requirements with the highest level of control?

options.text: Use AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) with Server-Side Encryption (SSE-KMS).
Use Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C) where the application manages the keys in local memory.
Use Amazon S3 Managed Keys (SSE-S3) for all bucket encryption.
Implement client-side encryption by encrypting objects locally within the application before uploading them to S3, using an unmanaged local keystore.

questions.explanation: AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) provide the ideal balance of security, control, and auditing. They enable security teams to craft precise key policies, enforce automatic annual key rotation, and track all decryption and encryption calls through AWS CloudTrail.

wrongOptionNotes.B: SSE-C places the burden of key management and secure storage entirely on the application, and does not integrate natively with AWS KMS auditing features like CloudTrail.
wrongOptionNotes.C: SSE-S3 keys are fully managed by AWS behind the scenes, offering no granular key policy control or manual key rotation to the customer's security team.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Client-side encryption without AWS KMS integration bypasses centralized cloud auditing and places excessive key management overhead on application developers.

questions.question: An organization is building a microservices architecture using Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. Services must communicate with each other securely within the VPC, and communication must be encrypted in transit using mutual TLS (mTLS). Additionally, incoming traffic from the Application Load Balancer (ALB) must be authenticated. Which solution provides the most secure and native implementation?

options.text: Deploy AWS App Mesh to manage service-to-service communication, leveraging sidecar proxies to automatically handle mTLS encryption and certificate rotation.
Configure standard security groups between ECS tasks to isolate traffic to specific ports.
Implement custom TLS certificate generation logic inside every application container and manually configure socket connections to perform handshakes.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to provision public certificates on the ALB and rely on standard HTTP communication between internal ECS tasks.

questions.explanation: AWS App Mesh uses Envoy proxy sidecars deployed alongside ECS tasks to manage network traffic. It natively supports mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication and encryption in transit between microservices without requiring developers to write custom certificate management logic.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Security groups provide network-level access control (firewall rules), but they do not encrypt data in transit or provide mutual TLS authentication.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Writing custom certificate management and handshake logic inside application code introduces significant security risks and operational overhead.
wrongOptionNotes.D: HTTP communication between internal microservices is unencrypted, failing the requirement for encryption in transit across the entire internal architecture.

questions.question: A global web application is deployed behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The security team needs to restrict access to the application so that users can only view content if they originate from specific corporate IP address ranges. All other requests must be blocked at the edge before hitting the origin servers. What is the most efficient way to implement this restriction?

options.text: Configure AWS WAF with an IP set matching the corporate IP ranges, and associate the Web ACL with the CloudFront distribution.
Update the CloudFront distribution's origin access control (OAC) settings to filter incoming viewer IP addresses.
Modify the application code running on the origin servers to inspect the 'X-Forwarded-For' HTTP header and reject unauthorized IP addresses.
Attach inbound IP-based security group rules to the Amazon CloudFront distribution edge nodes.

questions.explanation: AWS WAF integrates seamlessly with Amazon CloudFront. By creating an IP match condition rule within a Web ACL and associating it with the CloudFront distribution, requests from unauthorized IP addresses are blocked at the AWS edge locations, minimizing backend load and enhancing security.

wrongOptionNotes.B: Origin Access Control (OAC) is used to restrict access from CloudFront to the origin server (such as an S3 bucket), not to filter incoming viewer IP addresses.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Filtering at the origin server wastes compute resources processing unauthorized requests and incurs unnecessary data transfer costs to the origin.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon CloudFront edge nodes are managed by AWS and do not accept customer-managed security groups or inbound network ACL modifications.

questions.question: An enterprise has a multi-tier web application hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The security team needs to monitor the VPC for anomalous traffic, unauthorized port scans, and potential malware communication by analyzing raw IP traffic metadata. The solution must integrate with Amazon GuardDuty for automated threat detection. Which feature should the Solutions Architect enable?

options.text: AWS CloudTrail Event History
Amazon VPC Flow Logs
Amazon Inspector Network Reachability Assessments
AWS Trusted Advisor Security Checks

questions.explanation: Amazon VPC Flow Logs record IP traffic metadata passing through network interfaces in a VPC. GuardDuty can ingest and analyze VPC Flow Logs alongside DNS logs and CloudTrail events to identify malicious behavior such as port scans, unusual outbound communication, and compromised instances.

wrongOptionNotes.A: CloudTrail records API calls and control plane activities for AWS accounts, not network packet metadata or IP traffic within a VPC.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Amazon Inspector analyzes network configurations for potential reachability vulnerabilities to the internet, but does not ingest live VPC traffic flows for malware detection.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Trusted Advisor inspects the AWS environment for general security, cost optimization, and performance gaps, but does not provide real-time network traffic analysis.

questions.question: A financial services company is deploying an internal web application on Amazon EC2 instances. Employees must authenticate through the company's existing on-premises SAML 2.0-compliant Identity Provider (IdP) before accessing the web application. Which AWS service or feature should be used to integrate SAML authentication with minimal custom application development?

options.text: AWS Shield Advanced with custom authentication rules
Amazon IAM SAML identity providers combined with long-term IAM user credentials
AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO)
Amazon Cognito User Pools with custom Lambda triggers

questions.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center provides native integration with external SAML 2.0 identity providers (such as Microsoft Active Directory Federation Services, Okta, or Ping Identity). It enables secure single sign-on for employees accessing AWS-hosted applications and accounts.

wrongOptionNotes.A: AWS Shield Advanced is a managed DDoS protection service and does not handle user authentication or SAML federation.
wrongOptionNotes.B: IAM SAML federation grants access to the AWS Management Console or AWS APIs, not directly to an internal web application running on EC2 instances for employee login.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While Cognito supports SAML federated identities, it is primarily designed for consumer-facing (B2C) applications rather than internal corporate enterprise SSO integration.

questions.question: A healthcare enterprise requires that all objects uploaded to Amazon S3 must be automatically scanned for known viruses and malware before being processed by downstream applications. Which architectural pattern best satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 PutObject API calls and stream them to Amazon CloudWatch for malware inspection.
Attach an IAM resource policy to the S3 bucket that rejects uploads containing executable virus signatures.
Enable Amazon Macie on the S3 bucket to automatically quarantine files containing malware upon upload.
Configure an S3 Event Notification to trigger an AWS Lambda function that downloads the object, streams it through an antivirus scanning engine, and tags the object accordingly.

questions.explanation: An event-driven architecture using Amazon S3 Event Notifications combined with AWS Lambda is the standard pattern for custom object inspection. When an object is uploaded, the notification triggers a Lambda function that evaluates the payload against an antivirus scanning engine before allowing downstream processing.

wrongOptionNotes.A: CloudTrail logs metadata about API calls, not the binary content of files uploaded to S3, making malware scanning impossible through this method.
wrongOptionNotes.B: IAM policies evaluate user and resource permissions based on structural criteria (e.g., principal, action, condition keys), not the deep inspection of file contents for malware.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Amazon Macie discovers and protects sensitive data (like PII) using machine learning, but it does not perform antivirus or malware scanning on files.

questions.question: A company has an AWS environment spanning multiple AWS accounts managed through AWS Organizations. The security team needs to enforce a mandatory governance guardrail that prevents any user or role in member accounts from deleting specific critical Amazon S3 audit buckets, regardless of local IAM permissions. What is the most effective mechanism to enforce this rule globally?

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 Bucket Policies on each individual bucket to explicitly deny the 's3:DeleteBucket' action to everyone except the security account.
Apply cross-account IAM policies to all administrators in the member accounts.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to flag any attempts to delete critical S3 buckets and trigger an automated remediation script.
Create an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) with a deny rule for 's3:DeleteBucket' on the target resources, and attach it to the root or organizational units.

questions.explanation: AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) define the maximum available permissions for member accounts. By applying an SCP that explicitly denies destructive actions (such as 's3:DeleteBucket' or 's3:DeleteBucketPolicy'), the security team ensures that even account root users cannot override the governance guardrail.

wrongOptionNotes.A: While bucket policies can deny deletion, they must be managed individually on every bucket and can be bypassed if an administrator removes the policy.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Managing individual IAM policies across hundreds of users and accounts is cumbersome and prone to drift or accidental misconfiguration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Relying on reactive remediation (detect-then-correct) allows the deletion to happen initially, whereas prevention via SCPs stops unauthorized actions upfront.

questions.question: An application running on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access AWS services such as Amazon DynamoDB. The security team mandates that this traffic must not traverse the public internet, even via AWS public endpoints, to adhere to strict corporate compliance frameworks. Which AWS networking feature should be implemented?

options.text: A NAT Gateway deployed in a public subnet to translate private IP addresses to public IPs for AWS service calls.
An interface or gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon DynamoDB deployed within the VPC.
An Internet Gateway attached to the VPC with restricted security group outbound rules.
An AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection back to the corporate datacenter routing all AWS service traffic on-premises and back.

questions.explanation: VPC endpoints (Gateway endpoints for DynamoDB and S3, or Interface endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink for other services) allow resources within a private VPC subnet to communicate directly with AWS service APIs using private IP addresses inside the Amazon network, completely avoiding the public internet.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A NAT Gateway routes traffic over the public internet to reach public service endpoints, failing the requirement to keep traffic off the public internet.
wrongOptionNotes.C: An Internet Gateway enables communication over the public internet, directly violating the compliance requirement.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Routing AWS API calls through an on-premises datacenter via VPN introduces unnecessary latency and egress costs for intra-cloud communication.

questions.question: A multinational enterprise wants to ensure that all newly created Amazon S3 buckets across all accounts within their AWS Organization have public access blocked by default. What is the most scalable way to enforce this baseline security posture?

options.text: Write a cron job script running on an EC2 instance that periodically calls 'PutPublicAccessBlock' on all existing and new S3 buckets.
Rely on developers to manually check the 'Block public access' box during the bucket creation wizard in the AWS Management Console.
Configure AWS CloudTrail alerts to notify the security team whenever an S3 bucket is created without public access blocked.
Deploy an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) that enforces the 's3:PutAccountPublicAccessBlock' setting or denies bucket creation if public access block is disabled.

questions.explanation: AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) can be used to enforce security baselines across accounts. By crafting an SCP that restricts S3 operations or requires the S3 Block Public Access setting to be active, organizations prevent non-compliant resources from ever being provisioned.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Polling scripts are reactive, difficult to maintain, and leave a window of vulnerability between bucket creation and script execution.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Relying on manual user diligence inevitably leads to human error and compliance violations.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Alerting is purely detective and does not prevent non-compliant buckets from being created.

questions.question: An enterprise developer needs to connect to an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL database running inside a private subnet of a VPC for administrative troubleshooting. Security policies strictly prohibit exposing the database or bastion hosts directly to the internet. Which secure connectivity method should the Solutions Architect recommend?

options.text: Establish an AWS Client VPN endpoint without requiring authentication credentials for internal developers.
Modify the RDS database security group to temporarily allow inbound traffic from the developer's public IP address on port 5432.
Configure AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to establish a secure, audited shell connection to a management instance, combined with port forwarding to the RDS database.
Deploy a traditional bastion host (jump box) in a public subnet with SSH port 22 open to the developer's specific IP address.

questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure and auditable node management without needing to manage SSH keys, open inbound ports, or maintain public bastion hosts. Developers can securely tunnel database traffic through a private instance using port forwarding managed entirely via IAM policies.

wrongOptionNotes.A: While a Client VPN can connect developers to the VPC, unauthenticated VPN access is insecure and does not adhere to least-privilege principles.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Exposing a database port directly to the public internet, even temporarily, is a severe security violation and introduces high risk.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Traditional bastion hosts require open inbound ports (SSH/RDP) on the perimeter, creating a high-risk attack surface that violates modern security best practices.

questions.question: A security auditor discovers that an IAM role used by an automated deployment pipeline has overly permissive permissions, including 'iam:*' and 's3:*'. The security team needs to immediately restrict this role's maximum effective permissions without rewriting or breaking the underlying role definition or trust policy. What is the best feature to use?

options.text: AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs)
AWS WAF Web ACL rules
Amazon S3 Bucket Policies
IAM Permission Boundaries

questions.explanation: IAM permission boundaries are an advanced feature for defining the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to an entity. When applied to an IAM role, the effective permissions are the intersection of the identity-based policy and the permission boundary, allowing rapid containment of over-privileged roles.

wrongOptionNotes.A: SCPs apply to entire AWS accounts or organizational units, not to a single specific IAM role within an account.
wrongOptionNotes.B: AWS WAF filters web traffic at the application layer for HTTP/HTTPS requests on Application Load Balancers, API Gateways, and CloudFront distributions, not IAM API permissions.
wrongOptionNotes.C: S3 bucket policies apply to specific buckets and control access to data within those buckets, but they cannot restrict permissions across other AWS services like IAM.

questions.question: A financial company hosts a multi-tier application on AWS. Compliance auditors require proof that cryptographic keys used to encrypt sensitive data at rest are rotated regularly, and that any failure or deletion of keys generates an immediate alert. Which combination of AWS services provides this auditability and alerting capability?

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor security checks and Amazon Inspector vulnerability scans.
AWS WAF rate-limiting rules and VPC Flow Log analysis.
AWS KMS automatic key rotation combined with Amazon CloudWatch Alarms triggered by Amazon EventBridge rules capturing KMS CloudTrail events.
Amazon Macie data classification reports combined with AWS Shield DDoS metrics.

questions.explanation: AWS KMS supports automatic annual key rotation for customer managed keys. To monitor and alert on critical key actions (such as key scheduled deletion or disabling), security teams configure Amazon EventBridge rules to listen to AWS CloudTrail events from KMS and dispatch alerts through Amazon SNS or CloudWatch.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Trusted Advisor and Inspector scan configurations and software vulnerabilities, but do not actively monitor real-time KMS key lifecycle events or trigger alerts for key deletions.
wrongOptionNotes.B: WAF and VPC Flow Logs deal with network and web traffic security, not cryptographic key management or KMS audit logging.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Macie classifies sensitive data and Shield mitigates DDoS attacks; neither service monitors KMS cryptographic key rotation or lifecycle events.

questions.question: An organization is deploying an application that accepts file uploads via Amazon API Gateway and processes them using an AWS Lambda function. To prevent denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and excessive costs caused by malicious actors flooding the API with oversized payloads, what is the most effective security control to implement at the edge?

options.text: Write custom validation logic inside every downstream AWS Lambda function to check the incoming content length header.
Configure API Gateway payload size limits and associate AWS WAF with rate-limiting and size constraint rules.
Attach an Amazon VPC Security Group directly to the Amazon API Gateway endpoint.
Enable Amazon Inspector on the API Gateway deployment stage to automatically throttle malicious traffic.

questions.explanation: To protect serverless applications from volumetric floods and oversized payload attacks, integrating AWS WAF with Amazon API Gateway is the industry best practice. WAF allows defining rate-limiting rules, IP reputation lists, and size constraint conditions that inspect and filter requests at the edge before triggering backend compute.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Waiting until the Lambda function executes to check payload size still consumes compute resources and incurs invocation costs, failing to protect against DoS attacks.
wrongOptionNotes.C: API Gateway regional and edge-optimized endpoints do not accept direct attachment of VPC security groups.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Amazon Inspector evaluates network reachability and software vulnerabilities on EC2, ECR, and Lambda, but does not provide runtime traffic rate-limiting for API Gateway.

questions.question: A company is developing a web application hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The security team mandates that all incoming web traffic must be inspected for common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting before reaching the application. Which AWS service should the Solutions Architect integrate with the ALB to meet this requirement?

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS WAF
Amazon Inspector
AWS Shield Standard

questions.explanation: AWS WAF is designed to protect web applications by allowing you to create security rules that control access, filter web traffic, and block common attack patterns such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting when associated with an Application Load Balancer.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior, rather than inspecting web traffic at the application layer.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Amazon Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that scans AWS workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, not web traffic.
wrongOptionNotes.D: AWS Shield Standard provides automatic protection against common transport and network layer DDoS attacks, but it does not inspect application-layer web traffic for vulnerabilities like SQL injection.

questions.question: An enterprise is planning to migrate a sensitive database to Amazon RDS. Compliance regulations require that the database connection strings and credentials used by the application must be automatically rotated every 30 days without application downtime. Which solution meets these requirements securely?

options.text: Store the database credentials in an Amazon S3 bucket with server-side encryption and use an S3 Event Notification to trigger credential updates.
Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a SecureString and write a custom cron job on the EC2 instances to update the password.
Hardcode the credentials in the application configuration file stored in a private GitHub repository and update them manually every 30 days.
Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and configure automatic rotation using a built-in rotation Lambda function.

questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the optimal service for managing and automatically rotating database credentials. It integrates natively with Amazon RDS and uses AWS Lambda to execute the password rotation process securely.

wrongOptionNotes.A: S3 is not designed for managing dynamic database user credentials or handling secure password rotation natively.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While Parameter Store securely stores strings, it does not provide native automated rotation functionality comparable to Secrets Manager without complex custom orchestration.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Hardcoding credentials violates security best practices and manual rotation does not scale or meet compliance automation requirements.

questions.question: A company requires that its AWS environment complies with strict data residency requirements. The security team wants a centralized mechanism to continuously audit resource configurations across all accounts in AWS Organizations and automatically remediate non-compliant resources, such as publicly accessible S3 buckets. Which combination of services should the Solutions Architect use?

options.text: AWS IAM Access Analyzer and AWS CloudTrail logs analyzed via Amazon Athena
Amazon CloudWatch Events and AWS Trusted Advisor auto-remediation scripts
AWS Config with conformance packs and AWS Systems Manager Automation documents
AWS Shield and Amazon GuardDuty configured with custom security event rules

questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously assesses resource configurations. By combining AWS Config conformance packs with AWS Systems Manager Automation, organizations can achieve continuous compliance monitoring and automated remediation across multiple accounts in AWS Organizations.

wrongOptionNotes.A: IAM Access Analyzer helps identify unintended resource access, but it does not perform automated remediation or comprehensive configuration auditing across all AWS resources.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Trusted Advisor provides checks and recommendations, but it does not offer the granular configuration auditing and multi-account conformance pack remediation capabilities of AWS Config.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Shield and GuardDuty focus on threat detection and DDoS protection, not configuration compliance management or resource remediation.

questions.question: A media company is hosting confidential video assets in an Amazon S3 bucket. The security team needs to ensure that only authorized users within a specific partner company can stream these videos via Amazon CloudFront, and direct access to the S3 bucket objects via public URLs must be completely blocked. How should the Solutions Architect implement this?

options.text: Enable S3 Block Public Access and configure an S3 Bucket Policy that allows read access to any user presenting a signed CloudFront cookie.
Create an IAM user for the partner company and require them to include AWS Signature Version 4 credentials in every video request URL.
Configure the S3 bucket as a public static website and use AWS WAF on the bucket endpoint to restrict requests by IP address.
Configure CloudFront to use Origin Access Control (OAC) to access the S3 bucket, and remove all public access permissions from the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation: CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) is the modern, recommended mechanism to secure Amazon S3 origins. It restricts S3 bucket access solely to the specified CloudFront distribution, allowing public access to the S3 bucket to be completely disabled.

wrongOptionNotes.A: S3 bucket policies cannot natively parse or validate CloudFront signed cookies directly without an intermediary like Lambda@Edge.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Sharing IAM user credentials with external partners violates security best practices and does not integrate efficiently with standard video streaming clients.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Making the S3 bucket public contradicts the requirement to completely block direct public access to the bucket.

questions.question: An organization is deploying an application on Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC. The security team requires that all outbound traffic to the public internet from these instances must be routed through a centralized security appliance that performs deep packet inspection. The instances reside in private subnets. Which architecture fulfills this requirement?

options.text: Attach a NAT Gateway to each private subnet and configure security groups on the EC2 instances to filter outbound traffic.
Configure AWS Transit Gateway with an inspection VPC and rely on default security group outbound rules.
Configure custom route tables for the private subnets with a default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the elastic network interface of the security appliance instance.
Deploy an Internet Gateway directly in the private subnet and assign Elastic IP addresses to each EC2 instance.

questions.explanation: To route private subnet traffic through a security appliance, a custom route table must direct all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to the network interface of the security appliance or a Gateway Load Balancer.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A standard NAT Gateway routes traffic directly to an Internet Gateway without performing deep packet inspection or supporting third-party security appliance processing.
wrongOptionNotes.B: While Transit Gateway can route traffic to an inspection VPC, simple security group rules do not perform deep packet inspection.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Internet Gateways can only be attached to public subnets, and assigning public IPs exposes the private instances directly to the internet.

questions.question: A financial firm needs to ensure that all data stored in Amazon EBS volumes attached to Amazon EC2 instances is encrypted at rest using encryption keys managed by the company via AWS Key Management Service (KMS). Additionally, the company needs to enforce this encryption requirement globally for all new EBS volumes created in the AWS account. What is the most efficient way to achieve this?

options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function triggered by Amazon EventBridge to detect unencrypted volume creation and delete them immediately.
Enable 'Always encrypt new volumes' by default in the EC2 settings of the AWS region, and select the appropriate customer-managed KMS key.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to report on unencrypted volumes daily and manually encrypt them using snapshots.
Attach an IAM policy to all user roles denying the ec2:CreateVolume action if encryption parameters are omitted.

questions.explanation: Amazon EBS allows you to enable encryption by default for all new volumes created in an account per region. When enabled, EBS automatically encrypts new volumes using your specified customer-managed or default AWS managed KMS key.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Reactive deletion via Lambda is inefficient and disruptive; enabling EBS encryption by default prevents unencrypted volumes from being created in the first place.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Trusted Advisor is a reporting tool and does not provide proactive enforcement or prevention of unencrypted volume creation.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While IAM policies can restrict actions, managing explicit encryption parameters across all user roles is prone to gaps, whereas EC2 encryption by default provides native enforcement.

questions.question: An enterprise application running on Amazon EC2 instances requires access to various AWS resources, including Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB. To adhere to security best practices, the security team mandates that long-term credentials must not be stored on the EC2 instances. How should the Solutions Architect grant the necessary permissions?

options.text: Generate an IAM user with programmatic access, encrypt the credentials, and download them onto each EC2 instance securely.
Store an administrative access key pair in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and have applications retrieve them at startup.
Configure a VPC endpoint for AWS STS and use cross-account assumed roles for every API call made by the application.
Create an IAM role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the EC2 instances during launch or via the AWS Console.

questions.explanation: Using IAM roles for Amazon EC2 is the standard and most secure method to grant permissions to applications running on instances. AWS automatically rotates temporary security credentials provided to the instance via the Instance Metadata Service (IMDS).

wrongOptionNotes.A: Using IAM user long-term access keys violates AWS security best practices regarding credential management on compute instances.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Retrieving long-term access keys from Parameter Store still results in long-term credentials residing on the instance, violating the core security requirement.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Assuming cross-account roles manually adds unnecessary complexity when instance profiles natively grant permissions within the same account.

questions.question: A multinational corporation has multiple AWS accounts organized under AWS Organizations. The security architect needs to implement a preventive control that ensures no user or role in any member account can disable AWS CloudTrail logging, even if the user has administrator privileges. Which mechanism should the architect use?

options.text: Configure AWS Trusted Advisor alerts to notify the security team whenever CloudTrail status changes.
Attach an IAM permissions boundary to all administrator roles across every account that removes permissions to modify CloudTrail.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects CloudTrail disable events and triggers a Lambda function to re-enable logging.
Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the root level of AWS Organizations that explicitly denies the CloudTrail stop or delete actions.

questions.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations act as centralized preventive guardrails. An explicit deny statement in an SCP applies to all accounts within the organizational unit or root, preventing even account administrators from disabling critical security services like CloudTrail.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Trusted Advisor alerts are purely informational and do not prevent users from disabling CloudTrail.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Permissions boundaries must be attached to every user and role individually and can potentially be bypassed if administrators have permissions to modify boundaries.
wrongOptionNotes.C: EventBridge and Lambda provide reactive remediation, which leaves a window of time where logging is disabled, whereas an SCP provides a preventive control.

questions.question: An organization is building a multi-tier serverless application using Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that communication between the Lambda function and the DynamoDB table must not traverse the public internet. What is the most secure and efficient way to configure this connectivity?

options.text: Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet and route all Lambda database traffic through the NAT Gateway to the public DynamoDB endpoint.
Create a Gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB in the VPC and ensure the Lambda function is configured to run within private subnets associated with that VPC.
Set up an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the Lambda execution environment and the DynamoDB service endpoint.
Configure an Internet Gateway on the VPC and attach public IP addresses to the Lambda function execution environment.

questions.explanation: A Gateway VPC endpoint provides reliable, private connectivity to Amazon DynamoDB from within a VPC without requiring an internet gateway, NAT device, or VPN connection, keeping traffic entirely within the secure AWS backbone network.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A NAT Gateway routes traffic out to the public internet, failing the requirement that traffic must not traverse the public internet.
wrongOptionNotes.C: A Site-to-Site VPN is used to connect an on-premises datacenter to an AWS VPC, not for internal AWS service-to-service communication within the cloud.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Lambda functions do not support attaching public IP addresses directly, and an Internet Gateway exposes traffic to the public internet.

questions.question: A company is hosting a critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are distributed across multiple Availability Zones within a single AWS Region. The database runs on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL in a Multi-AZ deployment. The architecture must achieve a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of under 5 minutes and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of under 10 minutes in the event of an entire regional failure. Which architecture modification satisfies these requirements cost-effectively?

options.text: Rely solely on the existing Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and configure an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones behind the ALB.

Implement a pilot light disaster recovery architecture in a secondary AWS Region by replicating the RDS database via cross-region read replicas and keeping core application AMI templates updated, using Route 53 DNS failover.
Configure scheduled automated snapshots of the Amazon RDS database every 4 hours and replicate Amazon EBS snapshots of the EC2 instances to a secondary AWS Region using AWS Backup.

Deploy an active-active multi-region architecture using Amazon Aurora Global Databases with full capacity compute instances running in both regions simultaneously behind a latency-based Route 53 routing policy.

questions.explanation: For regional disaster recovery scenarios requiring low RTO and RPO without the high cost of active-active configurations, a pilot light or warm standby approach is ideal. Cross-region database replication ensures the RPO target is met, while automation tools allow rapid compute deployment to achieve the RTO target.

wrongOptionNotes.A: A Multi-AZ deployment provides high availability within a single region, but it does not protect against a catastrophic, region-wide disaster failure.
wrongOptionNotes.C: An RPO of under 5 minutes cannot be achieved with database snapshots taken every 4 hours, and EBS snapshot replication alone does not handle application state or database consistency adequately.
wrongOptionNotes.D: While this achieves near-zero RTO and RPO, maintaining full-capacity compute infrastructure in both regions is significantly more expensive than a pilot light or warm standby approach and exceeds the minimum requirements.

questions.question: An enterprise financial application runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application is stateless, but generating user session tokens is computationally expensive. During sudden traffic spikes, instances are overwhelmed before they can initialize local caches. How should a Solutions Architect redesign the architecture to ensure high availability and smooth traffic handling during scale-out events?

options.text: Offload session storage and frequently accessed lookup data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis, and configure an Amazon SQS queue to buffer incoming client requests.
Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) file system configured in Max I/O mode to all EC2 instances to store local application session state and caches.
Store user session data in Amazon ElastiCache for Redis shared across the Auto Scaling group, and use Amazon EC2 instance warm pools with pre-initialized application caches.
Increase the minimum and desired capacity of the Auto Scaling group to match peak load hours permanently, and scale up the instance types to larger sizes.

questions.explanation: To maintain high availability and prevent cold-start latency during scaling events, stateless applications should externalize session data to a managed in-memory store like Amazon ElastiCache, while using EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools to keep instances pre-warmed.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Using SQS introduces asynchronous queuing which is incorrect for synchronous web user session requests, even though ElastiCache is the correct choice for session state.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Amazon EFS provides shared storage, but file system latency and locking mechanisms are not optimal for high-performance session state management compared to in-memory caches like Redis.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Over-provisioning permanent capacity defeats the elasticity benefits of cloud architecture and drastically increases operational costs.

questions.question: A media streaming company stores its high-definition video catalog in Amazon S3. The company needs to design a resilient architecture that protects against accidental deletion, malicious overwrites, and region-wide disasters while optimizing storage costs. Which combination of features meets these criteria?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive for all video storage, enable cross-region replication to a secondary region, and disable S3 Versioning to avoid duplicate storage costs.
Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance mode, use Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for all objects, and configure AWS Backup to take daily snapshots.
Configure an Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Point, apply S3 Intelligent-Tiering to all buckets, and enable AWS CloudTrail logging for all S3 API calls.
Enable S3 Versioning, configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to a secondary region, and transition older videos to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval using S3 Lifecycle policies.

questions.explanation: Resiliency for S3 data requires versioning to protect against user error, cross-region replication for disaster recovery, and lifecycle policies to tier data down to lower-cost archive storage without sacrificing durability.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Disabling S3 Versioning removes protection against accidental deletion and overwriting, which violates the security requirement.
wrongOptionNotes.B: S3 Standard-IA is not cost-effective for long-term cold archives compared to Glacier, and Object Lock alone does not provide cross-region disaster recovery resilience.
wrongOptionNotes.C: While Multi-Region Access Points route requests efficiently, they do not inherently protect against accidental deletions unless versioning is enabled, and CloudTrail only logs API activity rather than protecting data.

questions.question: A global e-commerce platform runs its core transaction processing tier on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL in a Multi-AZ configuration. During peak shopping events, read-heavy queries originating from analytics dashboards cause high CPU utilization on the primary database instance, impacting checkout processing speeds. How can a Solutions Architect decouple analytics traffic to ensure high availability and performance for transactions?

options.text: Migrate the analytics reporting workload to an Amazon DynamoDB table that is asynchronously synchronized via AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
Configure Amazon ElastiCache in front of the primary Aurora database to cache all incoming SQL queries and database responses.
Implement Amazon Aurora Auto Scaling for the primary writer instance so it can dynamically scale up its CPU and memory resources during high-traffic events.
Deploy multiple Amazon Aurora Read Replicas across different Availability Zones and configure the analytics application to connect to the reader endpoint.

questions.explanation: Aurora Read Replicas distribute read traffic across multiple low-latency endpoints across Availability Zones, decoupling heavy read-only analytical queries from the primary transactional writer instance.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Migrating to DynamoDB introduces unnecessary data modeling complexity and synchronization overhead when Aurora natively supports scalable read replicas.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Caching complex analytics queries in ElastiCache is inefficient due to frequent cache invalidations and does not scale out complex analytical processing effectively.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Aurora writer instances cannot scale vertically automatically without downtime or failover actions, and vertical scaling is not a substitute for read scaling.

questions.question: An enterprise application deployed on Amazon EC2 instances spans two AWS Regions to ensure high availability. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS service. The architecture requires that normal user traffic be routed to Region A, but if health checks fail in Region A, traffic should automatically failover to Region B. Additionally, 10% of test traffic should be routed to Region B regardless of health status for canary deployments. Which Route 53 routing policy configuration should be implemented?

options.text: Configure a Latency-based routing policy with Route 53 health checks enabled for both regional resource records.
Configure a Geoproximity routing policy with bias parameters adjusted to favor Region A while spilling over excess traffic to Region B.
Configure a Failover routing policy for Region A as primary and Region B as secondary, and layer a Weighted routing policy on top to direct 10% of traffic to Region B.
Configure a Multi-Value Answer routing policy with randomized responses weighted at a 90/10 ratio between the two regions.

questions.explanation: Route 53 supports complex routing configurations by combining routing types. A Failover routing policy ensures disaster recovery readiness, while weighted routing enables controlled traffic percentages for testing.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Latency-based routing routes traffic based on the lowest network latency to the user, not primary/secondary failover with a specific canary traffic split.
wrongOptionNotes.B: Geoproximity routing relies on geographic locations and bias adjustments, which does not provide deterministic failover or a precise 10% canary split.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Multi-value answer routing returns up to eight healthy records randomly and does not provide deterministic primary/secondary failover behavior.

questions.question: A financial services firm runs a mission-critical legacy monolith application on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The company cannot rewrite the application to be stateless immediately, but business continuity policies dictate that the application must recover automatically from underlying hardware failures or instance crashes within minutes without manual intervention. What is the most resilient and cost-effective architectural design?

options.text: Configure an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replicate the instance's root volume continuously to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Place the EC2 instance inside an Auto Scaling group with a minimum, maximum, and desired capacity set to 1, and configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to reboot the instance if status checks fail.
Create a warm standby EC2 instance in another Availability Zone and use an AWS Lambda script to switch the elastic IP address when a failure is detected.
Migrate the application to an AWS Lambda function with provisioned concurrency configured to handle execution latency.

questions.explanation: Using an Auto Scaling group with a capacity of 1 is a cloud design pattern for single-instance legacy applications. It guarantees self-healing capabilities against underlying host failures by automatically replacing unhealthy instances.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Storage Gateway does not provide automated failover or automated provisioning of replacement EC2 instances upon failure.
wrongOptionNotes.C: Custom Lambda scripts for health checking and manual IP shifting introduce potential split-brain risks, delay, and maintenance overhead compared to native Auto Scaling.
wrongOptionNotes.D: Legacy monolith applications typically cannot run inside AWS Lambda without significant architectural refactoring.

questions.question: A company is designing a mission-critical web application that relies on an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The database must remain available even if an entire Availability Zone experiences a major outage. Furthermore, if the primary database instance fails, a failover to a replica must occur automatically with minimal interruption. Which database architecture fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Deploy two Amazon Aurora instances in the same Availability Zone and use active-active clustering software configured over shared block storage.
Deploy a single Amazon Aurora MySQL instance with automated daily snapshots and cross-region replication enabled to a secondary AWS Region.
Deploy an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ instance and attach an AWS Lambda function to promote read replicas upon detecting database connection errors.
Deploy an Amazon Aurora Multi-AZ deployment with one primary writer instance and two Read Replicas deployed across three distinct Availability Zones.

questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Multi-AZ architecture distributes compute instances across multiple Availability Zones while utilizing a distributed, fault-tolerant, self-healing storage volume spanning three AZs, ensuring high availability and fast automated failover.

wrongOptionNotes.A: Deploying instances in the same Availability Zone provides zero protection against an AZ-level outage.
wrongOptionNotes.B: A single instance does not provide high availability within the same region during an Availability Zone failure, and daily snapshots do not provide rapid automated failover.
wrongOptionNotes.C: RDS Multi-AZ handles failover natively; writing custom Lambda functions for failover is redundant and increases the risk of split-brain errors.

questions.question: A multi-tier web application runs behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributing traffic to EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones. During a database migration, the database experiences high latency, causing the backend web tier to exhaust its connection pool and stop responding to health checks. The ALB marks all instances unhealthy and stops routing traffic, causing a total outage even though instances are running. How should the architecture be modified to improve fault tolerance and graceful degradation?

options.text: Replace the Application Load Balancer with a Network Load Balancer (NLB) operating at Layer 4, which does not evaluate application-level health checks.
